identity.name: Santos-Dumont

case.bezel: flat sapphire crystal, no bezel (rectangular case)

identity.one_liner: The closest current-catalog descendant of Cartier's 1904 Santos, built to the original's thin rectangular proportions rather than the sportier automatic Santos de Cartier.

narrative.story: In 1904, the aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont complained to his friend Louis Cartier that a pocket watch was impractical to check mid-flight; Cartier's response was a flat-cased wristwatch with a distinctive square bezel, generally cited as Cartier's first men's wristwatch and one of the earliest wristwatches purpose-built for a man rather than adapted from a pocket watch. The current Santos-Dumont keeps closer to those slim, elongated proportions than the automatic Santos de Cartier, which was redesigned sportier in 2018.
narrative.collector_notes: Santos-Dumont references split between steel quartz models like this one and gold or platinum manual-wind pieces on higher calibers; confirm movement type and case material specifically, since the name alone does not fix either.
